decisions.decision: The five-member framing is an ATTRIBUTION ERROR at nine measured sites, not merely an underivable count.
decisions.rationale: Oracle consult, CONFIRMED by end-to-end reads of five parts: the book NEVER states five and explicitly states FOUR in prose, because its rundown folds two members into one bullet. Five is a reading of the hierarchy figure only; counting from the catalog's variations run yields six or nine instead. So the count is attributed to the figure rather than to the author as his framing, the numeral is kept because the figure supports it, and the caveat that his prose says four is ADDED -- that caveat is exactly the what-you-may-not-cite content this document should carry. Same defect class as the fabricated mapping this remediation exists to remove, repeated nine times.

decisions.rationale: The consult reported four table rows are non-members (an umbrella and three variations), which sounded like it needed a level column or a table split -- trap-quadrant, since it would ripple through every cell bullet, every derived count and the guard work. MEASUREMENT showed the document's convention is to state the relationship in the defining-property cell and it already does so for THREE of the four. Only one row lacks it. Fix that cell; change no table structure. Also measured: the other families the consult warned might be flattened have ZERO rows and ZERO mentions, and the alias collision it flagged is not live here.

decisions.decision: No search capability for either oracle agent; a sweep is the driver's or harness's job.
decisions.rationale: Reviewed NOT SAFE. rg --pre and rg --hostname-bin each run an arbitrary program and both match an rg prefix, so no prefix rule can preserve read-only; the frontmatter pattern is advisory regardless. Granting it would move writes-nothing from a tool-layer guarantee to a promise, in the one agent trusted to hold copyrighted text and whose own threat model anticipates injected instructions inside that text. Two further reasons: the low-leak forms recommended (-c/-l) are precisely a compilation dump, since store filenames are numbered descriptive slugs that together render the table of contents; and the sibling gate requires negatives confirmed by complete read, so sweep-certified absences would stall its converge-to-clean loop. The sibling's own contract already assigns deterministic checks to the harness.

Reviewers briefed from scratch keep finding what primed ones miss -- the wholly unprimed reviewer found the most this round, including two blocking defects neither other reviewer saw. MY OWN ERRORS THIS SESSION, all caught: I claimed a frontmatter tools pattern would scope Bash to one command (it is advisory, and rg can exec arbitrary programs anyway, so the claim was wrong twice); I recommended -c/-l as the low-leak search forms when they are the compilation dump; I wrote an absence rule telling the agent to name the unread remainder with no firewall qualifier, introducing a compilation-leak vector into the very section warning about overclaiming; I relayed a -uu gotcha from the global instructions that is false, then verified it properly only when asked; and earlier I raised a false alarm that live checker topics survived when a crude grep simply could not tell a positive topic from an absent guard. The pattern in every case: a control or claim that reports success without verifying the thing it names.
